summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission, post-transplant graft-versus-host disease, systolic heart failure, and chronic kidney disease, was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and near syncope at home. He was found to have acute on chronic heart failure with pulmonary edema and bilateral pleural effusions, leading to hypoxic respiratory failure. Treatment with intravenous furosemide improved his symptoms, though his renal function temporarily worsened, requiring careful management. His metabolic acidosis resolved, and imaging ruled out pulmonary embolism or infection. A non-contrast cardiac MRI showed severe left ventricular dysfunction without evidence of myocardial inflammation or iron overload. He was stabilized on home diuretics, with plans to initiate outpatient dialysis and follow-up with nephrology, cardiology, and pulmonology. He was discharged home with improved oxygenation and stable vital signs, continuing all baseline medications.
